six_dimensional_cards.title: F1: permission to maintain precedes permission to read

dimensions.trigger: Servers concurrently interpret shared data using different schema versions.
dimensions.problem: A reader can use a new index while an older writer omits its maintenance, producing incorrect answers.
dimensions.mechanism: Preserve both adjacent versions’ invariants; adding an index passes through delete-only and write-only permissions before readers may use it. Permit only one version of lag, advance at most once per lease period, and reject expired-schema writes at storage commit. Begin backfill only after delete-only writers lose commit eligibility and every eligible writer maintains the index; expose reads after reorganization.
dimensions.limits: The proof assumes F1’s shared transactional storage, schema interpretation and lease/commit machinery. Application deployment versions do not automatically inherit it. Lock-coverage changes need their own timestamp-preservation protocol.
dimensions.counterexample: Waiting for a server’s refresh timer does not prevent its paused, expired-schema write from committing later.
dimensions.verification: Proposed: pause a writer across the version boundary, mutate and delete indexed rows during reorganization, and compare index answers with a base-data oracle. Verify rejection at the protected commit, not only a refresh log.

six_dimensional_cards.title: gh-ost: controllability and cutover are separate contracts

dimensions.trigger: A live MySQL table needs a structural change while serving writes.
dimensions.problem: Migration work competes with serving traffic, and an apparently finished copy may omit subsequent mutations.
dimensions.mechanism: Tail row-based binary logs into an altered shadow table; serialize copying and event application. Throttle migration writes and postpone cutover while continuing catch-up when appropriate. Replica test mode freezes replication for original/shadow comparison.
dimensions.limits: Historical motivation is not a current MySQL capability matrix. Replica tests do not reproduce all primary contention or application-version behavior.
dimensions.counterexample: Successful row copying does not prove the shadow is caught up, or that old application SQL accepts the new schema.
dimensions.verification: Proposed: include concurrent update/delete, pause/resume, binlog backlog and a long transaction obstructing cutover. Compare transformed rows at a common source boundary, plus foreground outcomes and acknowledged writes.

six_dimensional_cards.title: Shopify: schema publication is a fleet-wide application boundary

dimensions.trigger: A Rails application uses cached schema metadata while shards complete migrations independently.
dimensions.problem: An arbitrary shard can supply a schema that other shards do not yet serve. Reverse replication can also encounter a uniqueness violation when events from different shards arrive in a different order.
dimensions.mechanism: Keep changing columns out of generated application SQL during transition; publish a schema-cache dump only after every shard completes and no competing migration remains. Verify future routing/transaction constraints before sharding.
dimensions.limits: `ignored_columns` affects Active Record’s model SQL, not every handwritten SQL path or external writer. The account’s reverse-replication error concerns a specific resharding flow, not every schema migration.
dimensions.counterexample: Merely retaining the old database does not establish a usable rollback target after new writes diverge or reverse replication stops.
dimensions.verification: Proposed: vary shard completion order, restart a process with a cached schema, and exercise direct SQL. For a reversible traffic switch, inspect reverse-stream progress and reconcile post-switch acknowledged mutations before declaring recovery available.

assumptions: Every original V0 business writer already increments source_rev in the same local transaction; every row creation has an immutable, non-reused source_incarnation.
V1 writes both representations and matching source_rev/mapped_rev atomically in one database.

Backfill reads one consistent row snapshot, then conditionally updates an existing row by observed source_incarnation AND source_rev; it cannot insert a deleted row. V2 reads all compatibility fields in one consistent row snapshot.
Version floor must be enforceable at actual commit/write boundary or unsupported transactions must be proven drained.
Actual engine supplies schema/index publication and selected snapshot/log comparison semantics.

stages.instruction: **Expand without exposing.** Add nullable `status_code` and `mapped_rev` using the selected engine’s supported algorithm. Keep both columns out of application-generated SQL during partial shard completion. Observe actual schema on every required shard before a bridge begins writing them; do not publish a cache from whichever shard answers first.

**Introduce V1 bridge writers.** In one local transaction, write the old text, new code, next `source_rev`, and matching `mapped_rev`. V0 may still write only text and increment `source_rev`; a mapped value can therefore become stale even when non-null.

**Run a bounded backfill.** Read text, incarnation and revision in one consistent row snapshot; compute the code, and conditionally update the still-existing row only when both `source_incarnation` and `source_rev` match that observation. Set `mapped_rev` to that revision. On mismatch, reread/reconcile. Do not insert a row that disappeared. Track required source membership, coverage and catch-up; a cursor’s end alone is insufficient.

**Allow V2 readers with a compatibility rule.** Read text, code and both revisions in one consistent row snapshot. Use a supported, non-null code only when non-null `mapped_rev == source_rev`; otherwise derive the answer from authoritative text. Keep predicates on a path that includes stale/unmapped rows. An index on code alone cannot find rows whose text changed under V0 but whose code did not.

**Close the V0 writer boundary.** Stop new admission and account for queued jobs, retry/replay entry points and open transactions. Enforce the chosen version floor at the actual write/commit boundary or prove those writers drained. A deployment percentage and an expired process heartbeat do not prove this. Complete the final reconciliation and the engine’s index publication checks before code-only predicates become authoritative.

**Keep a rollback-compatible interval.** V2 reads the new representation; V1 still maintains both. Preserve the old readers’ supported values and old schema while their rollback/replay contract remains active. Keep rollback writers behind the V1 bridge. If rollback must reactivate V0-only writers, first restore V2’s text fallback and stop code-only predicates; otherwise retain the writer floor. Rehearse old code against post-switch writes.

**Retire deliberately.** Only after old readers/writers and recovery dependencies are accounted for may V3 stop maintaining the old text and remove it. Record that accepting a new value such as `archived → 2`, which V0 cannot interpret, or destroying the old representation changes the recovery options.

original_rehearsal.oracle: Independent fixture ledger of definitively committed business operations, transaction identities, authoritative incarnations/revisions, rejected attempts, and manually specified expected statuses/deletions. Record acknowledgements and reconcile unknown outcomes; response arrival is not commit order. No migration transformation code, success flags or sampled equality. Freeze fixture writers at reconciled committed H or use supported common snapshot/log boundary. Enumerate expected AND actual base/index identities/values. Require exact set equality in both directions, including missing, extra/resurrected and orphan entries; then compare query answers.

scenarios.schedule: Backfill reads pending/revision 1; V0 commits paid/revision 2; old backfill resumes
scenarios.required_observation: Old conditional update affects zero rows. V2 returns paid through the compatibility path; later reconciliation maps revision 2.

scenarios.schedule: Backfill reads row B; V0 deletes B; backfill resumes
scenarios.required_observation: No resurrection; B is absent from all authoritative answers at H.

scenarios.schedule: Backfill reads B/incarnation X/revision 1; delete and recreate B/incarnation Y/revision 1; old backfill resumes
scenarios.required_observation: Incarnation comparison rejects the old result. New B’s acknowledged value survives; equal revisions alone cannot authorize an update.

scenarios.schedule: V1 commits a new status/revision; an older copy is replayed
scenarios.required_observation: Acknowledged new value survives; the oracle matches both representations when their revisions match.

scenarios.schedule: One shard completes before another; a new process refreshes its cache
scenarios.required_observation: New-column exposure remains gated; ordinary requests do not depend on a schema absent on another required shard.

scenarios.schedule: V0 pauses before commit, then resumes after the version floor
scenarios.required_observation: The protected boundary rejects the unsupported write, or verified draining establishes that no such transaction remains. No success acknowledgement is invented.

scenarios.schedule: Concurrent unique-index build fails, or table-swap attempt times out
scenarios.required_observation: Inspect engine state and query/write behavior. Failed build status alone does not prove constraints are absent; failed cutover does not imply writes stopped.

recovery_limits: Old application code must still understand post-switch values/schema.

After code-only reads become authoritative, keep rollback writers behind V1 bridge or restore V2 fallback and stop code-only predicates before permitting V0-only writes; otherwise preserve the writer floor.
Bridge interval maintains both representations but does not make every transform invertible.
Widened type then out-of-range value, or removed unique constraint then duplicates, can defeat schema reversion.
Old retained table needs post-cutover acknowledged-write catch-up; reverse-stream status and ordering constraints matter.
Once recovery route closes choose compatible forward repair or scoped restore/replay; recreating a column does not recover discarded values.

engine_index_gate_schedule.scope: Historical F1-style engine protocol, separate from application representation backfill with V2 fallback.
engine_index_gate_schedule.schedule: Pause delete-only writer across planned backfill entry.
engine_index_gate_schedule.required_observation: Backfill entry remains blocked while writer may commit without index insertion. Once writer loses commit eligibility and all eligible writers maintain index, allow entry; resumed expired-schema commit must fail.
